head: db321e6df06fb3b800e0f0896d832c36278c2195
classification_reasons: Spec tightness: the spec is tight (every flagged concern decided, acceptance measurable), but the build departs from it once: the four workflow timeout comments of R4 are proposed in evidence/workflow-comments.md instead of written, recorded in plan.md Risks.

Blast radius: 48 files across the gate (checks, gate, artifacts, limits), the runner (run_phase step budget, session caps at (e)), auto_round, triage, the PR body, collect.py, init detection, three skills, two agents, three commands and the template sdlc.yaml; the gate record gains a `proof` entry in every (c), (d) and (e) record and a fourth `drive` run. This is a contract change that R19 will read.

Test coverage: the new paths are new code with new tests (tests/test_proof.py and additions to ten test files). The existing tests of the runner's step are kept untouched. The only edited pre-existing test (tests/test_policy_skills.py, ux check) follows a behaviour change the spec asks for (R11: images under proof/ and screenshots/, not evidence/ directly), and it is extended, not weakened.
attempted: Intent: I checked every Proposed-outcome bullet against the diff: the fourth optional target and its two variables, the runner's step at (c)/(d)/(e) and never (b), drive.log, clearing proof/, the manifest, red drive as a decision-29 round, the drive kept out of commands_from_config/recheck/recheck_targets, job-time arithmetic (300 s default, 600 s cap, (e) subtraction), the proof-item grammar, judging against the approved plan, the drive-removed park, the image caps, the two folders, /sdlc-test step 3, the verifier step, reviewer angle 9, the PR evidence line, triage logs, Playwright detection, the four-log lists, and the version bump. All are present. The change solves the stated problem, not a nearby one.

Spec and plan: the diff stays inside plan.md's 'Files that change'. It adds two files to that list in (c): evidence/workflow-comments.md and .claude-plugin/marketplace.json, which version-check requires. All four workflow templates are absent from the diff, as the departure says. Spec R16 itself says this repository's workflow copies stay untouched, and tests/test_templates.py:334-346 and :662-666 require those protected copies to equal the rendered templates byte for byte. So the departure is the only consistent reading, not a skipped requirement. The exact lines are handed to the owner.

Proof: at (c) there are no test.log, build.log or lint.log. That is allowed: REQUIRED_EVIDENCE at (c) is verifier.md only, and the runner runs the suite after this session. evidence/verifier.md exercises the changed behaviour through direct calls: the grammar, strict_equal, compare_state, run_drive with the caps and the manifest, judge_proof, check_proof (deferred / not checked / drive removed / no drive), check_evidence's drive-log deferral, red_targets, the job-time table, init detection and collect.py --only drive. It names what it did not exercise: run_deferred_commands end to end, evidence_status, Windows. Those paths are covered by the tests in the diff (test_the_runner_s_step_runs_the_drive_after_the_targets_and_judges_the_proof, test_a_drive_that_did_not_start_is_re_run_once_on_a_fresh_proof_folder, test_no_drive_runs_at_b, test_pr additions). I ignored the runner records (run-c.json, hook-log).

Blast radius (runner step): I read plugin/gate/gate.py:529-669. The drive runs after run_targets only when drive_from_config is set and the phase is c/d/e. The not_started re-run calls run_targets(only=['drive']), which yields {} (checks.py:441-443), and then re-runs run_drive, which clears proof/. A crash on the first attempt resets runs and re-runs everything. _judge_proof_after replaces only a deferred `proof` entry. A drive that did not run gives a failure without items, so it never becomes a round. The record's check order is kept. No regression on the no-drive path: the `proof` entry is ok at once and never deferred, so deferred_checks is unchanged for such projects.

Blast radius (auto_round): red_targets was split into _red_runs and _red_proof. The old early returns are kept: a deferred, missing, crashed or not-started commands entry still returns None. A failed proof entry with approved failing items is a round even when commands is green. It parks when drive_removed is set, when there are no items, or when only unapproved items failed. The evidence-on-red-logs acceptance now includes drive.log through target_logs(True). head_matches delegates to gitops.only_change_folder_moved, a verbatim lift of the old body.

Blast radius (time): commands_timeout_seconds(config, gate_phase) caps at 600 unless gate_phase is 'e'. Both readers in the step pass gate_phase: run_gate_commands receives gate_phase as its `phase` (run_phase.py:3512, :2319), and step_budget is computed at :3528. run_caps and run_timeout_seconds subtract drive_minutes only when gate_phase is 'e'. compose passes `model_phase or phase` (:2102), and model_phase=gate_phase (:3284). gate_phase is st.phase for a fix round and the run's phase otherwise (:3129), so the review pass ('review') keeps its whole cap. check_limits subtracts the same drive_minutes when ctx.phase is 'e'. build_caps_minutes_needed passes nothing and gets the capped figure. One harmless observation: at (b) the step's wait still counts the drive's timeout, though no drive runs there. This only lengthens a bound, and spec R4's formula does not exclude (b).

Blast radius (callers and shapes): evidence_status gained a root parameter, and its three callers (description bullets, pr/cli.py check_run_result, release/notes.py _evidence_line) all pass it. description.py already imports checks, gitops, json and load_sdlc_config (lines 54-74). limits.py now imports gate.checks at module level, while checks imports limits lazily inside functions, so there is no import cycle at load time. No risk-list item, no schema, migration or deployment config, and no guardrail file (.claude/**, CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md, sdlc.yaml, .github/workflows) is in the diff. template/sdlc.yaml is project content, not the guardrail.

Policies: security baseline. The drive's environment is drive_env(os.environ + 2 vars), and inside the runner os.environ is commands_env() (run_gate_commands env=commands_env()), so no token or model credential is added. Proof paths are kept inside proof/ (.. refused, linked_part, resolved-prefix check). The item regex comes from the owner-approved plan and runs on a file capped at 1 MiB. Data conventions: the template comment requires synthetic data, and the manifest records commit and run. UX: every new park has a need text that says what to do. Definition of done and ux-conventions skill texts were corrected to match the code.

Tests: could the tests pass with the bug still present? I checked these cases. strict_equal at depth, with [true]/[1] and {a:1}/{a:1.0}. A missing drive.log is deferred in CI while a missing test.log still fails and a by-hand drive.log is missing. A red drive gives drive (exit 1). A differs gives seen 500. A dropped image is not produced. The re-run's proof/ lacks the first run's file. No drive runs at (b). The no-drive path keeps three runs and today's reason. Each has a test that asserts the observable value, not only a truthy result. The only pre-existing assertion changed is the ux check's finding text. Its new test keeps the old negative case (an image directly under evidence/ is no longer accepted, by design) and adds both folders. This is not a fix-type change, so the test lock does not apply.
Skip markers: I read the test diff and found no skip, skipif or xfail marker added. None declared in plan.md, none needed.

Claims against today's code: I checked these claims and found each true: run_targets(only=...) (checks.py:432); not_started's 126/127 rule (gate.py:406-421); GateContext.approved_artifact falling back to the working tree when there is no base (checks.py:143-154); gate_setting (checks.py:156); build_context(any_phase=...) (gate.py:163-181); artifacts.linked_part (artifacts.py:379); detect.node_dependencies and node_setup (detect.py:624, :180); _no_target (detect.py:96); compose's model_phase (run_phase.py:2079); and the two template tests the departure cites (test_templates.py:334, :642), which require byte equality with the protected copies. The plan's claim that check_evidence failed a missing log before its deferral branch matches the removed lines in the diff; the new branch is placed before the missing test, for drive.log only.

Edge I looked for and judged not a reason: after a round on a red drive at (d) or (e), the fix session's collect.py writes no mark for drive.log. The session's own gate can then read the previous run's red drive.log and fail `evidence` in the in-session record. The runner's step always rewrites drive.log at (d)/(e) (`written` is non-empty) and re-judges `evidence`, so the final record and the round logic are correct. Only the session's own interim view is red, and no reader acts on it before the step.
The drive (angle 9): this change adds no project drive of its own; commands.drive is empty here, so there is no drive file to read for reading versus writing values.
